extraction.notes: Whole study read. Extracted the study's findings, conclusions and recommendations on labour mobility (Open Balkan Initiative, emigration of Macedonian workers, wage differentials with Serbia as a driver of worker movement) and the description of the Open Balkan labour market memorandum. Left out: the general literature review on global and EU migration not about North Macedonia or the Western Balkans (pages 9-14), data for 2016 and earlier (Table 2.1, visa facilitation from 2005), general labour-market statistics and occupational gap figures with no stated link to mobility (sections 3 and 5.1 to 5.2 except the sentences that link them to mobility), data tables, methodology and references. ICT occupations are mentioned often (shortage of ICT professionals, Serbian ICT sector); judged incidental to the technology theme because technology is not the object of the claims (they concern workers in a sector), so these items carry no theme code. Speaker is Finance Think unless the text attributes the claim to another body.

items.stated_text: As part of the initiative, several memoranda, agreements and common declarations have been signed so far, among which the Memorandum of Cooperation related to the free access to the labor market in the Western Balkans, through reduced employment barriers among the countries, electronic application for obtaining identification number and facilitation of administrative procedures for obtaining a temporary residence permit.
items.summary: Under the Open Balkan Initiative a memorandum was signed on free labour market access, including electronic application for an identification number and simpler residence procedures.
items.intervention_as_stated: Memorandum of Cooperation related to the free access to the labor market in the Western Balkans
items.extraction_note: Status from 'have been signed so far'. TECH-DGOV for the electronic application procedure for obtaining an identification number. Subjects taken from the preceding sentence naming the three Open Balkan countries. No signature date is stated.

items.stated_text: It stipulates that every resident of the signatory countries has the right to free movement, residence and work in the territory of the three countries. In order to ensure equal access for all residents of these countries, the signatories should simplify the procedures for entry, residence and work in their countries.
items.summary: The memorandum gives residents of the signatory countries the right to move, reside and work in all three, and obliges signatories to simplify procedures.
items.intervention_as_stated: Memorandum of Cooperation related to the free access to the labor market in the Western Balkans
items.extraction_note: Describes the content of the memorandum in the previous item; status as stated there ('signed').

items.stated_text: Before or at the latest 90 days after entering of the neighboring country, residents of the contracting countries should register in order to obtain a permit for free access to the labor market for a period of two years, with the possibility of its extension. The permit includes the right to employment without a work and residence permit for foreign nationals, but excludes the possibility of using state subsidies for employment, such as the existing active labor market programs and measures (Finance Think, 2023).
items.summary: Residents must register within 90 days for a two-year renewable labour market access permit, without work or residence permits, excluding state employment subsidies.
items.intervention_as_stated: Memorandum of Cooperation related to the free access to the labor market in the Western Balkans
items.extraction_note: Describes the content of the memorandum; status as stated in the first memorandum item ('signed'). The study cites its own earlier policy brief.

items.stated_text: While the existing analyses confirm that the economic integration initiatives increase the labor mobility, there is a scarce firm evidence on the impact of the regional initiatives on the labor markets of the WB countries (ILO, 2021; Anukoonwattaka and Heal, 2014; Baldwin and Venables, 1995).
items.summary: Analyses confirm integration initiatives increase labour mobility, but firm evidence on regional initiatives' impact on Western Balkan labour markets is scarce.

items.stated_text: Whether simplified employment rules in these countries under the OBI umbrella will make them more attractive than EU countries depends on the wage levels in the destination country as the most significant factor affecting labor mobility..
items.summary: Whether simpler Open Balkan employment rules make these countries more attractive than EU countries depends on destination wage levels.

items.stated_text: The intraregional mobility in the six countries of the Western Balkan remained stable from 1995, accounting for 15% of the total migrants from these countries.
items.summary: Intraregional mobility among the six Western Balkan countries has stayed stable since 1995 at 15% of their total migrants.

items.summary: Emigration of Western Balkan citizens outside the region rose 10% in ten years; in 2021 about 4.77 million lived abroad.

items.summary: In 2020 nearly 700,000 citizens of North Macedonia lived outside their country of birth, 30% more than 20 years earlier.

items.summary: In 2021 over 16,000 citizens of North Macedonia obtained valid EEA permits; 52% for family reunification and 28% for employment.

items.summary: Migrants from North Macedonia in Slovenia and Croatia mostly seek better employment and earnings; elsewhere family reasons dominate.

items.summary: In 2021 about 4,000 citizens of North Macedonia obtained first EEA permits for employment, half of them in Croatia and Slovenia.

items.stated_text: Compared to five years ago, the map of the Macedonian labor migrant has significantly changed, by bringing Croatia and Slovenia to the top, as the most attractive countries for temporary employment.
items.summary: Compared with five years earlier, Croatia and Slovenia have become the most attractive destinations for temporary employment of Macedonian labour migrants.

location.section: 2.2 Labor mobility in a regional integration context

items.stated_text: Although there are no official data, for example, a large part of our migrants in recent years leave and work in the hospitality sector in Croatia.
items.summary: Without official data, the study states that many recent migrants from North Macedonia work in hospitality in Croatia.

items.stated_text: Despite the further reduction of the unemployment rate, the activity and employment rates have stagnated and noted even a slight decrease, likely due to the increased flows to inactivity, due to discouragement for finding a work (triggered during the hit of the COVID-19 pandemic), but also due to their emigration to other countries in search for better employment (Figure 3.2).
items.summary: Since the pandemic activity and employment rates stagnated, likely due to discouragement and emigration in search of better employment.
items.extraction_note: Kept because the source links the trend to emigration of workers; hedged ('likely').

items.stated_text: These rates even deteriorated compared to a decade ago, both for the workforce with primary and secondary education, which signalizes that the deactivation and possible labor mobility more frequently occurred among the low-educated and low-skilled workers.
items.summary: Falling activity and employment among primary and secondary educated workers signals that deactivation and possible labour mobility were more frequent among low-skilled workers.

items.stated_text: The highest job vacancy rate has been recorded in 2022 compared to the previous years, which may indicate an increased labor mobility due to the post-pandemic openness of the economies. The rate of job vacancies has been continuously among the highest in the accommodation and food services, which may further signalize on labor mobility (Table 3.2).
items.summary: The record 2022 job vacancy rate, highest in accommodation and food services, may indicate increased labour mobility after the pandemic.

items.stated_text: Besides the active jobseekers, there are more than 47 thousand people who are passive jobseekers, i.e. they are not registered with ESA, due to detachment from the labor market, informal work, or (possibly) emigration to another country.
items.summary: More than 47,000 passive jobseekers are not registered with the Employment Service Agency, owing to detachment, informal work or possibly emigration.

metric.indicator: Passive jobseekers not registered with the Employment Service Agency

items.extraction_note: Reference period taken from the paragraph's opening sentence on 2022 jobseekers.

items.stated_text: As the Open Balkan Initiative is a three-lateral project of North Macedonia, Serbia and Albania, it is expected that the planning regions bordering the other two countries would benefit the most of the initiative for free labor mobility.
items.summary: The planning regions bordering Serbia and Albania are expected to benefit most from the Open Balkan free labour mobility initiative.

location.section: 3.2 The labor markets of the bordering planning regions

items.stated_text: In the context of OBI, the eased labor mobility between the neighboring countries may worsen the medium-skill occupational gap, given that more than half of the labor migrants from North Macedonia possess medium skills (OECD, 2022).
items.summary: Eased Open Balkan labour mobility may worsen the medium-skill occupational gap, as most labour migrants from North Macedonia have medium skills.

location.section: 5.1 Occupational gaps at the national level

items.stated_text: Also, the remarkable development and growth of the ICT sector’s contribution to the GDP in Serbia in the last years, more than 5% (Mara and Landesmann, 2022) may attract our ICT workers, further exacerbating the existing occupational gap.
items.summary: Growth of Serbia's ICT sector may attract ICT workers from North Macedonia, worsening the existing occupational gap.

location.section: 5.1 Occupational gaps at the national level

items.stated_text: However, EU countries have traditionally host the most of the labor migrants, despite some changes in destinations, while the intra-regional mobility has remained low. Hence, significant changes in such destination structure can be expected if there are significant differences in the earning prospects, an issue we discuss in section 5.3.
items.summary: EU countries host most labour migrants and intraregional mobility is low; destination changes would need significant differences in earning prospects.

location.section: 5.1 Occupational gaps at the national level

items.stated_text: The deficit among the tertiary educated is the largest among information and communication technology professionals due to the large need for developers (442) and software testers (53), and a very limited supply of only 13 graduated information professionals (Table 5.5). The last may be further deepened as a result of the eased labor mobility within OBI, considering the fast growing ICT industry in neighbouring Serbia.
items.summary: Skopje's largest tertiary-level deficit is ICT professionals, which eased Open Balkan mobility may deepen given Serbia's growing ICT industry.
items.extraction_note: Two sentences quoted together because the second ('The last') refers back to the first.

items.stated_text: Due to the proximity of the Skopje and North-East regions to neighboring Serbia, the facilitated labor mobility may cause a distortion of the regional labor markets for ICT occupations. The galloping development of this industry in Serbia, offering better employment opportunities, may increase the already existing deficit for ICT workers in both regions.
items.summary: Facilitated mobility may distort Skopje and North-East ICT labour markets, as Serbia's growing ICT industry may deepen their deficits.

items.stated_text: Due to the limited labour demand in the Polog region, the eased labor mobility may steer the large pool of unemployed to emigrate in search of employment in Albania, considering that two-thirds of the citizens of Polog are ethnic Albanians who will not face any language barriers.
items.summary: Eased mobility may lead many unemployed in Polog to seek work in Albania, as most are ethnic Albanians without language barriers.

items.stated_text: Yet, the latter may be a disadvantage for the labor mobility of the citizens of the South-West region, where almost half are ethnic Macedonians.
items.summary: Language may be a disadvantage for labour mobility of South-West region residents, almost half of whom are ethnic Macedonians.
items.extraction_note: 'The latter' refers to language barriers in the previous sentence (previous item).

items.stated_text: The second major group, Professionals, recorded a statistically significant and negative result which suggests that wages in North Macedonia are lower compared to wages in Serbia, by 6.1% for science and engineering professionals, up to around 14% for health and social professionals and 23.8% for IT professionals.
items.summary: Professionals earn significantly less in North Macedonia than in Serbia: 6.1% less in science and engineering up to 23.8% for IT.

metric.indicator: Wage differential for professionals, North Macedonia compared with Serbia

items.stated_text: Тhe latter may further deepen the shortage of IT professionals in North Macedonia, while the lower wages for 14% may steer the pool of unemployed health and social professionals to seek employment in Serbia.
items.summary: Lower wages may deepen the IT professional shortage and steer unemployed health and social professionals to seek work in Serbia.
items.extraction_note: The first letter of 'The' in the text file is a Cyrillic look-alike (U+0422); copied as it stands in the text file.

items.stated_text: However, the estimated wage differentials for these occupations are statistically insignificant, suggesting that we cannot expect an increased inflow of Serbian workers who would fulfil the shortage of workers in North Macedonia.
items.summary: Wage differentials for clerical support workers are insignificant, so no increased inflow of Serbian workers to fill shortages is expected.

items.stated_text: Medium-skilled service and sales workers are paid more in North Macedonia, especially personal care workers who receive almost 50% higher wages than workers in Serbia. The Open Balkan initiative can result in greater mobility of these workers from Serbia to North Macedonia, hence reducing their shortage.
items.summary: Service and sales workers, especially personal care workers, earn more in North Macedonia; the Initiative may draw them from Serbia, reducing shortages.

items.stated_text: However, the previous estimations showed that in North Macedonia, there is deficit of building workers only, and the higher salary of 9.5% can, to a certain extent, encourage Serbian workers to relocate in North Macedonia.
items.summary: Building workers, the only craft occupation in deficit, earn 9.5% more in North Macedonia, which may encourage Serbian workers to relocate.

items.stated_text: The positive wage differentials for all low-skill occupations are encouraging, hinting that higher wages in North Macedonia may attract workers from Serbia, who will fill the significant shortage of these workers.
items.summary: Higher low-skill wages in North Macedonia may attract Serbian workers to fill significant shortages.

items.stated_text: The wages for food preparation assistants are nearly 25% higher, which may be a trigger to fill the shortage of these workers, especially during the summer season, when Macedonian workers move to work in more developed countries like Croatia.
items.summary: Food preparation assistants earn nearly 25% more, which may help fill shortages, especially in summer when Macedonian workers go to Croatia.

items.stated_text: High-skill occupations in the borderline regions are generally not paid differently between the two countries, or slightly less than in Serbia for two occupations, which indicates that there is no premium wage to encourage labor mobility.
items.summary: In border regions high-skill wages barely differ between North Macedonia and Serbia, so there is no wage premium encouraging mobility.

items.stated_text: An important difference when compared to the national level is recorded for the wages of the IT workers: IT professional and technicians in the borderline regions of North Macedonia receive 37% and 21.6% higher wages, respectively, although the national data showed a reverse trend.
items.summary: In border regions IT professionals and technicians in North Macedonia earn 37% and 21.6% more than in Serbia, unlike national data.

metric.indicator: Wage differential for IT professionals and IT technicians, border regions of North Macedonia compared with Serbia

items.stated_text: This is probably driven by the higher wages that IT companies in the Skopje region pay, and may cause a significant inflow of Serbian IT workers from the borderline places to the IT companies based in Skopje.
items.summary: Higher IT wages in Skopje may cause a significant inflow of Serbian IT workers from border areas to Skopje companies.

items.stated_text: The need for customer care clerks in the Skopje region is high; 68 workers are needed for each job vacancy. At the same time, the wage for these workers in the borderline regions in the county is 17.7% higher in North Macedonia, opening the possibility of attracting workers from Serbia.
items.summary: Customer care clerks are in high demand in Skopje and earn 17.7% more in border regions, possibly attracting workers from Serbia.

items.stated_text: The results for wage differentials in low-skill occupations are the same as those at the national level, suggesting that Macedonian workers are paid more than those in Serbia. This could encourage the movement of labor but also the engaging of the domestic unemployed labor force with ‘no designated occupation’.
items.summary: Low-skill workers are paid more in North Macedonia than in Serbia, which could encourage labour movement and employment of domestic unemployed.

items.stated_text: The Initiative, as an opportunity for regional economic integration with our neighbors, is extremely important for the Macedonian economy and should enable a faster structural adjustment to the challenges brought by the open labor market. The Initiative’s effect on the domestic labor market depends on its current state, but also on the desire of policymakers to conduct structural changes.
items.summary: The Open Balkan Initiative is very important for the economy; its labour market effect depends on current conditions and policymakers' will for structural change.

items.stated_text: On the other side, six of eight low-skill occupations are in deficit (lower supply than demand), which is particularly pronounced for service and elementary workers. The latter is probably due to the frequent emigration of these workers to other countries in search of higher earnings, but also a reflection of the notion that there is a large contingent of individuals with no designated occupation, who are frequently with low or no education, but who do not fill at least some of these gaps.
items.summary: Six of eight low-skill occupations are in deficit, probably due to emigration for higher earnings and unemployed without occupation not filling gaps.

items.stated_text: Seen from the perspective of the regional integration and labor mobility, the advantages of the OBI would be fulfilling the shortages of workers, especially in the borderline regions.
items.summary: From a mobility perspective, the Open Balkan Initiative's advantage would be filling worker shortages, especially in border regions.

items.stated_text: However, calculations showed that in neighboring Serbia the salary premium is very small, almost insignificant, and hence, it is not expected that the destination will be chosen for relocation of Macedonia workers. However, for sectors that are seasonal in nature and cyclical in need of workers, differences in wages may appear, and this may cause additional pressure on already existing occupational gaps, like those in elementary occupations.
items.summary: Serbia's wage premium is almost insignificant, so Macedonian workers are not expected to relocate there, except possibly in seasonal sectors.

items.stated_text: The OBI needs to be a stimulus for faster conduct of the structural reforms for addressing the existing labor market gaps and a starting point in the eventual opening of the labor market upon accession to the EU.
items.summary: The Open Balkan Initiative should speed structural labour market reforms and prepare for opening the labour market upon EU accession.

items.stated_text: An efficient policy coherence and participative dialogue between economic, educational and social stakeholders should take special care of the labor market, in order to avoid future rise of the existing gaps.
items.summary: Coherent policy and dialogue among economic, educational and social stakeholders should prevent labour market gaps from growing.

items.stated_text: Adjusting labor market policies to prevent increase of the workers in the surplus occupations, who, unable to find suitable employment, emigrate to the neighboring countries or further:
items.summary: Labour market policies should be adjusted to prevent growth of surplus occupations whose workers emigrate to neighbouring countries or further.
items.extraction_note: Heading of a group of recommendations; the bullet points that follow are separate items.

items.stated_text: Regular monitoring of the occupational shortages or surpluses through deeper survey of the demanded skills needs and the labor force survey to identify deficit/surplus of certain occupations.
items.summary: Occupational shortages and surpluses should be monitored regularly through deeper skills needs surveys and the labour force survey.
items.extraction_note: Not tagged TECH-DATA: improving surveys without reference to data systems is incidental under themes.csv.

items.stated_text: Designing active labor market policies for appropriate qualification of workers without occupation into at least elementary workers. ESA, together with the service providers that offer program verification and/or further qualification, should design and deliver verified training courses and modules to the workers without occupation, and equip them with qualifications suitable for at least the low-skill occupations.
items.summary: Active labour market policies should qualify workers without occupation; ESA and training providers should deliver verified courses for at least low-skill jobs.

subjects.name_as_stated: service providers that offer program verification and/or further qualification

items.stated_text: Business sector should enable more numerous and more intense on-the-job training opportunities for the workers without designated occupation.
items.summary: Businesses should offer more and more intensive on-the-job training for workers without a designated occupation.

items.stated_text: Intensifying the labor market services for career counseling and guidance of the secondary school entrants into the VET schools, in order to decrease the supply of workers that are currently in a surplus, like science and engineering associate professionals and legal, social and cultural professionals.
items.summary: Career counselling for students entering VET schools should be intensified to reduce supply of surplus occupations.

items.stated_text: Creating tailor-made educational policies to steer creation of workers in the deficit occupations, reducing the need for import of foreign workers and preventing that their prospective import plagues domestic unemployed into a very long-term unemployment:
items.summary: Educational policies should produce workers for deficit occupations, reducing need to import foreign workers and preventing long-term unemployment of domestic unemployed.
items.extraction_note: Heading of a group of recommendations; the bullet points that follow are separate items.

items.stated_text: Activating the Skills Forecasting Observatory as a starting point for increasing attractiveness and quotas of deficit occupations.
items.summary: The Skills Forecasting Observatory should be activated to increase attractiveness and quotas of deficit occupations.

items.stated_text: Intensifying the activity of the Centers for qualification, retraining and verification, with the aim of adequate retraining of unemployed workers without designated occupation who can fulfill the deficit of workers in the elementary occupations.
items.summary: Centres for qualification, retraining and verification should step up retraining of unemployed without occupation to fill elementary occupation deficits.

subjects.name_as_stated: Centers for qualification, retraining and verification

items.stated_text: Designing educational curricula that reflect the labor market needs, and intensifying the participation of the business sector in the design process.
items.summary: Curricula should reflect labour market needs, with greater business sector participation in their design.

items.stated_text: Narrowing the gaps in the labor markets of the planning regions, through providing more employment opportunities in the domestic economy and reducing the need for emigration in search for employment in the (neighbouring) countries:
items.summary: Regional labour market gaps should be narrowed by creating domestic jobs and reducing the need to emigrate for work.
items.extraction_note: Heading of a group of recommendations; the bullet points that follow are separate items.

items.stated_text: Increasing the attractiveness among the large companies and foreign investors that create new job vacancies, through providing preferential services in the regions/municipalities where the labor demand is low and limited.
items.summary: Large companies and foreign investors should be attracted with preferential services in regions and municipalities with low labour demand.

items.stated_text: Directing potential investors in technological industrial zones located in regions with a large number of unemployed persons (e.g. Polog region), with the aim of more balanced regional development.
items.summary: Investors should be directed to technological industrial zones in regions with many unemployed, such as Polog, for balanced regional development.
items.extraction_note: Not tagged with a technology theme: 'technological industrial zones' is an investment location, technology is not the object of the claim.
